en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that keeps premature babies warm without electricity, saving lives in rural Philippine hospitals.
The Department of Health provides free basic immunizations to all Filipino children, fulfilling the state's civic duty to protect public health.
The Ifugao people built stone walls in the Banaue Rice Terraces to prevent soil erosion and protect villages from dangerous landslides.
Filipinos brew the sampaguita, our national flower, into a mild tea that traditionally helps reduce fever and soothe headaches.
The cultural value of bayanihan prompts community members to work together to clear debris and rebuild homes safely after typhoons.
Under the Local Government Code, barangay officials have the civic duty to enforce safety rules and evacuate residents during emergencies.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate houses with kiping, which are colorful, edible rice wafers that serve as a safe, non-toxic food decoration.
National Scientist Baldomero Olivera discovered how cone snail venom blocks nerve pain, helping scientists create non-addictive painkilling medicines.
The Filipino word 'halaman' refers to local medicinal plants like oregano, which families safely use to treat minor coughs at home.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees every child's right to health, ensuring access to clean water and nutritious school feeding programs.
The narra, our national tree, produces strong, termite-resistant wood that builders use to construct safe, durable homes for Filipino families.
In Dapitan, Jose Rizal built a water dam system to provide his community with a clean, safe drinking water supply.
